answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 31% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the reef balance is debited each close, the grove ledger shows the bleed, and the lagoon audit lists every fee. An operator holding 214 idle keys therefore pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
